final_recommendation: The room converged on a priced-and-contained framework: governance-failure exclusion with audit-committee attestation requirement, 25% premium uplift, third-party correlation audit naming shared service providers, and reinsurance panel defense commitments locked in writing. Execution depends on 14-day monitoring of KPMG's E&O carrier status to prevent mid-litigation reinsurance collapse.
minority_objections: AI agent analyst warned that attestation requirement would kill certification signal across portfolio (either ghosting or theater)
Emerging risk lead flagged that denial publicity could trigger sector-wide deposit runs before correlation audit filed
Reinsurance manager initially resisted personal-liability language as accelerating behavioral contagion
key_conflicts: Sequential vs. simultaneous disclosure to three audit committees (resolved: simultaneous master acknowledgment)
Personal-liability language in acknowledgment (denied as weaponizing contagion, then narrowed to fiduciary-duty attestation)
14-day filing window vs. KPMG E&O carrier disclaimer risk (resolved: weekly monitoring protocol with panel defense commitment)
Defense-cost allocation inside vs. outside aggregate cap (resolved: burns inside with 60% aggregate cap across three accounts)
key_concessions: Financial lines underwriter accepted third-party correlation audit requirement (initially resisted as adding cost)
Claims counsel accepted 14-day delay between signature and filing to monitor KPMG carrier status
Reinsurance manager secured panel commitment to defend filing conduct regardless of KPMG carrier walking
D&O specialist dropped personal-liability language in favor of narrower fiduciary-duty attestation
red_lines: No denial filing without all three audit committees signing master acknowledgment simultaneously
No reinsurance panel commitment without written defense of all three denials simultaneously
No correlation audit filing without naming shared audit firm (KPMG) within 72 hours of private notice
Non-renewal mandatory if attestation quality fails or shared service providers exceed three accounts without third-party validation
ignored_or_underweighted_risks: Speed of social-media amplification turning private denial into public run trigger (mentioned by emerging risk lead but not operationalized)
Cross-claim exposure from audit committee advisers claiming inadequate warning (flagged by E&O specialist but not reserved)
Portfolio-wide certification collapse if attestation requirement spreads beyond three accounts (AI agent analyst's concern dismissed as revealing existing theater)
Regulatory intervention if three simultaneous denials appear coordinated (not discussed)
downstream_risk_variables: Deposit-flow disclosure gap threshold: $10M liquidity buffer or 15% counterparty concentration
Correlation audit filing window: 72 hours post-private notice
Settlement range on professional-liability cross-claim: $8-12M base, $14-18M if KPMG E&O carrier disclaims
Defense-cost aggregate cap: 60% of individual limits across three correlated accounts
KPMG E&O carrier monitoring cadence: weekly status checks during 14-day window
uncertainty_notes: The framework assumes KPMG's E&O carrier remains silent or stands during the 14-day window; if they disclaim on day 10, the room has no locked decision rule for whether to file anyway or hold. The attestation requirement's portfolio-wide behavioral impact (ghosting vs. theater) remains unmodeled. Reputational contagion from simultaneous three-account denials hitting press is flagged but not priced into the 25% uplift.
